prompt: Review an unseen sanitized AI-enabled production architecture and security packet. Defend its operation and harm contract, threat model, content and instruction boundaries, data/model/retrieval supply chain, generated-output handling, tool authorization, isolation, approvals, secrets, privacy, adversarial evaluation, audit, kill paths and incident recovery. Recover one reviewer-injected injection, poisoning, leakage, unsafe-tool or artifact incident, prove the bounded user and system postconditions independently, and revise the design after a material tenant, data, model, tool, regulatory, latency, availability or cost constraint changes.
deliverables: User operation, actors, assets, trust assumptions, prohibited effects, harm severity, fallback, residual-risk owner and explicit non-goals.
End-to-end trust-boundary and data-flow diagram covering user, application, context, model, validation, tool broker, approval, downstream enforcement, audit and kill path.
Threat model distinguishing direct and indirect prompt injection, jailbreak, retrieval/data/model poisoning, output injection, excessive agency, leakage and supply-chain compromise.
Content-origin, trust-class, ingestion, transformation, quarantine, retention and deletion controls for prompts, files, web content, datasets, labels, embeddings, indexes and caches.
Immutable release and supply-chain evidence for source, dataset, model, tokenizer, prompt, policy, tools, dependencies, image, builder, signature, provenance, SBOM or ML-BOM and admission decision.
Typed output and tool schemas, semantic validators, sink-specific encoding, target constraints, idempotency, deadlines, rate/concurrency limits and complete mediation.
Authenticated subject/tenant propagation, least-privilege tool identities, downstream authorization, secret handles, audience, expiry and cross-tenant isolation evidence.
Approval design binding exact preview, digest, target, effect, approver, separation of duties, expiry, nonce, revalidation and commit receipt.
Sandbox and workload-isolation design covering process, filesystem, network, credentials, resource limits, escape response and evidence limits.
Threat-model-derived adversarial suite with per-technique denominators, critical slices, invariants, false decisions, escaped-attack containment, downstream outcomes and independent review.
Structured decision and effect audit with trace/decision IDs, policy revision, redaction, access, integrity, retention, deletion, dropped-event and investigation contracts.

Independent kill, credential revocation, route deny, queue drain, egress block, propagation/acknowledgement, incident scope, eradication, recovery, regression, changed-constraint defense and exact cleanup.
evidenceRequirements: Reviewer supplies unfamiliar synthetic architecture, identities, policies, content, artifacts, provenance, tool calls, approvals, queues, traces, audit records and downstream state.
No real credential, customer data, shared production service, unrestricted shell, external model endpoint, broad cloud or cluster authority, external effect or unknown cleanup.
Every claim binds authenticated subject, tenant, content origin, immutable release, policy/tool version and relevant event or commit time.
The model transcript is never accepted as proof of authorization, committed effect, containment, deletion or user outcome.
Detector metrics remain separate from deterministic authorization, approval and downstream-effect metrics with explicit denominators and attack slices.
Artifact digest, signature, signer/issuer trust, provenance, vulnerability evidence, format safety and behavioral evaluation are treated as different claims.
Approval is invalid when the preview, authority, target, state, expiry or committed bytes change.
Audit evidence is useful for reconstruction while secrets and sensitive content are minimized, masked, access-controlled and lifecycle-managed.
The kill mechanism operates without model cooperation and every queued or in-flight action has a reconciled disposition.
Reviewer observes incident containment, credential and queue handling, downstream recovery, changed-constraint revision, independent postconditions, delayed recall and cleanup.
